rationale:
Split into four children. All four are existing comparator-accepted declarations, reused under the same names with byte-identical frozen types, so no new DAG node is created.

Why this split:
(1) Same type as an accepted twin. The selected type is byte-identical to that of the accepted twin node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.im_local-a1.glue-a1 (cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local_reps; candidate b43f7a042b; isolated comparator passed). The two supplied natural proofs and plans differ only in their provenance and node-id lines, so the mathematics and step numbering are identical.
(2) The twin's children are all accepted. Its reviewed decomposition used exactly the four children proposed here: cover_refine, imrep_local_finite, orient_union and glue_pieces. Each is now accepted with a candidate commit and a passing isolated comparator (3ca4b60601, 702e7082a5, 294e024b53, 03f646da67).
(3) Reuse passes the runtime gates. Each of the four names is owned by exactly one DAG node, and that node's lean_statement is byte-identical to the one proposed here. So the reuse passes _existing_lean_name_problem and _accepted_checkpoint, and _solve_children maps each key to the existing accepted node.
(4) Why not reuse the twin itself or skip the split. The twin glue declaration cannot be a child: it has exactly the parent's type, which would be a circular restatement. Not splitting would force this node to re-formalize about 150 lines of already-accepted Lean inline.

What each child covers. These are genuine, reusable obligations of the supplied proof:
(a) cover_refine: steps 2–3 (Lindelöf plus disjointed), stated for an arbitrary property p.
(b) imrep_local_finite: the local finiteness used in steps 6(b) and 7(γ).
(c) orient_union: step 7 ((IMC)(a) applied in W_i and in U, then a countable union).
(d) glue_pieces: steps 4–6 and 8. These give the glued carrier and multiplicity, the identity μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ, local integrability, measurability of ξ, and the glued IMRep with orientation ξ and weight μ.

Step 1 (U = ∅) needs no separate child: cover_refine returns ι = Empty, and glue_pieces glues the empty family.

How the children prove the parent. The assembly also uses the parent's existing dependency imrep_measure (cbr_imRep_measure_basic).
(a) Apply cover_refine with p(W) := ∃ R : IMRep W k, μ⌞W = R.measure ∧ ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, y ∈ W → ξ y = R.orient y. The last hypothesis of the parent is exactly cover_refine's premise. Choose the R_i.
(b) μ((⋃_i A_i)ᶜ) = μ(Uᶜ) = 0.
(c) μ⌞A_i = (μ⌞W_i)⌞A_i = (R_i.measure)⌞A_i, because A_i ⊆ W_i (Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset).
(d) ξ = ξ_i holds R_i.measure-a.e. (rewrite R_i.measure = μ⌞W_i and use ae_restrict_iff' with W_i Borel). Then it holds Hᵏ⌞M_i-a.e. by imrep_measure's Hᵏ⌞M_i ≪ R_i.measure (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le), and hence Hᵏ⌞(M_i ∩ A_i)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).
(e) glue_pieces then gives R' : IMRep U k with R'.orient = ξ and R'.measure = μ.
(f) For ω ∈ TestFormOn U k, imrep_measure's last conjunct gives R'.action ω = ∫ R'.orient(ω) dR'.measure = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = X ω. So R' represents X.

subproblems.title: Countable disjoint Borel refinement of a local open cover (Lindelöf)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) be any set, and let p be any property of subsets of ℝ^P. Suppose every x ∈ U lies in an open set W ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ W, W ⊆ U and p(W). Then there are a countable index type ι (ι : Type with Countable ι; ι may be empty) and families (W_i)_{i∈ι}, (A_i)_{i∈ι} of subsets of ℝ^P such that: every W_i is open, W_i ⊆ U and p(W_i) holds; every A_i is a Borel set with A_i ⊆ W_i; the A_i are pairwise disjoint; and ⋃_i A_i = U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (p : Set (Euclid P) → Prop), (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W ∧ x ∈ W ∧ W ⊆ U ∧ p W) → ∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Countable ι) (W A : ι → Set (Euclid P)), (∀ i, IsOpen (W i)) ∧ (∀ i, W i ⊆ U) ∧ (∀ i, p (W i)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (A i)) ∧ (∀ i, A i ⊆ W i) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (A i) (A j)) ∧ ⋃ i, A i = U
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the selected node's supplied proof, stated for an arbitrary property p of the covering sets instead of the IMRep data. Step 2 is the countable subcover (Lindelöf; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). Step 3 is the disjoint pieces A_i := W_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} W_j (Mathlib disjointed). The case U = ∅ of the supplied step 1 is absorbed by allowing an empty countable index type. Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P, with its Euclidean topology (second countable) and its Borel σ-algebra.

1. (Choice of neighbourhoods.) By hypothesis, every x ∈ U has an open V_x ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ V_x, V_x ⊆ U and p(V_x). Choose one such V_x for every x ∈ U. (In Lean, choose! gives V : ℝ^P → Set ℝ^P with these four properties for every x ∈ U.)

2. (The chosen sets cover U.) Index the chosen sets by the points of U (the subtype ↥U): s(x) := V_x. Every s(x) is open, and ⋃_{x∈U} V_x = U. The inclusion ⊆ holds because each V_x ⊆ U. The inclusion ⊇ holds because each y ∈ U lies in V_y.

3. (Lindelöf.) ℝ^P is second countable. So for the family (s(x))_{x∈↥U} of open sets there is a countable set of indices T ⊆ ↥U with ⋃_{x∈T} s(x) = ⋃_{x∈↥U} s(x) (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). By step 2 both unions equal U.

4. (Case T = ∅.) Then U = ⋃_{x∈∅} s(x) = ∅. Take ι := Empty, a countable type with no elements, and let W and A be the empty families (Empty.elim). Every condition quantified over i holds vacuously, and so does pairwise disjointness. Finally ⋃_i A_i = ∅ = U.

5. (Case T ≠ ∅: enumeration.) T is countable and nonempty, so T = range f for some f : ℕ → ↥U (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range). Put ι := ℕ, which is countable, and W_n := s(f(n)) = V_{f(n)}. Since f(n) ∈ U, step 1 shows that W_n is open, W_n ⊆ U and p(W_n) holds.

6. (Disjoint Borel pieces.) Put A := disjointed W, i.e. A_n = W_n ∖ ⋃_{j<n} W_j. Then:
(a) each A_n is Borel, being built from the open, hence Borel, sets W_j by finitely many set operations (MeasurableSet.disjointed);
(b) A_n ⊆ W_n (disjointed_subset);
(c) the sets A_n are pairwise disjoint (disjoint_disjointed);
(d) ⋃_n A_n = ⋃_n W_n (iUnion_disjointed).

7. (The pieces cover U.) ⋃_n W_n = ⋃_n s(f(n)) = ⋃_{x ∈ range f} s(x) (biUnion_range) = ⋃_{x∈T} s(x) = U by step 3. With step 6(d), ⋃_n A_n = U.

8. (Conclusion.) If T ≠ ∅, steps 5–7 give all seven required properties with ι = ℕ. If T = ∅, step 4 gives them. ∎

subproblems.title: Local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞M and of the weight of an integer multiplicity representation
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (an IMRep U n). That is: M = R.carrier is Borel with M ⊆ U; θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M; and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let μ_R = R.measure = θ·(Hⁿ⌞M), i.e. (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U: Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ and μ_R(K) < ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the local-finiteness facts used in steps 6(b) and 7(γ) of the selected node's supplied proof. For compact K ⊆ W_i, Hᵏ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M_i∩K} θ_i dHᵏ < ∞, because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i and R_i is locally integrable. This is the standing hypothesis of Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–747): the multiplicity θ is a locally Hⁿ-integrable positive integer-valued function. In the frozen contract it is encoded by the IMRep fields mult_pos and locallyIntegrable_mult.

Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P (Euclid P); M = R.carrier; θ(x) = R.mult x ∈ ℕ ⊆ [0, ∞]; μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U.

1. K is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, hence Borel (IsCompact.measurableSet).

2. (Weight of K.) Since K is measurable:
- μ_R(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M), by the definition of withDensity (withDensity_apply);
- (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict).
Hence μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ, after commuting the intersection.

3. The IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set K ⊆ U, gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞. By step 2, μ_R(K) ≠ ∞. This is the second conclusion.

4. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) For x ∈ M ∩ K, the field mult_pos gives 0 < R.mult x in ℕ. Hence 1 ≤ R.mult x, and after casting to [0, ∞], 1 ≤ θ(x).

5. (Measurability.) θ is measurable. It is the composition of the measurable map R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ (field measurable_mult) with the cast ℕ → [0, ∞], and every map out of the discrete space ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat).

6. (Unweighted measure.) Hⁿ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHⁿ (setLIntegral_one). This is at most ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by monotonicity of the set lower integral (setLIntegral_mono), using the pointwise bound of step 4 on M ∩ K and the measurability of step 5. The right side is finite by step 3, so Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞. This is the first conclusion. ∎

subproblems.title: Orientation is local: a countable union of Borel pieces of IMRep carriers is oriented by ξ
subproblems.statement: Assume (IMC)(a), passed as a hypothesis. It is the first hypothesis of the selected node dmcbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local_reps: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and all Borel sets M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x iff it is one of M' at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt). Let ι be a countable type, P, k ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. For each i ∈ ι let W_i ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let R_i be an IMRep in W_i (IMRep (W i) k) with carrier M_i and orientation ξ_i, and let N_i be a Borel set with N_i ⊆ M_i. Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k) and M := ⋃_i N_i. Assume M ⊆ U, Hᵏ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hᵏ = μHE[k]), and, for every i, ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) for Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ N_i. Then for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P such that Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q) and ξ(x) orients Q (IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the selected node's supplied proof, stated for an arbitrary countable family of Borel pieces N_i ⊆ M_i. That step orients the glued carrier: (α) the field orients of R_i; (β) ξ = ξ_i a.e. on the piece; (γ) (IMC)(a) in W_i; (δ) (IMC)(a) in U; and the countable union via ae_restrict_iUnion_iff.

Notation: Hᵏ := μHE[k]. For i ∈ ι write M_i := (R i).carrier and ξ_i := (R i).orient, and put M := ⋃_i N_i.

The hypotheses are those of the statement: (IMC)(a); ι countable; U open; every W_i open; every N_i Borel with N_i ⊆ M_i; M ⊆ U; Hᵏ(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; and, for every i, ξ = ξ_i holds Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e.

The proof uses the sibling imrep_local_finite (rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top): for any set W, any R : IMRep W k and any compact K ⊆ W, Hᵏ(R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ and R.measure K ≠ ∞.

1. (Reduction to one piece.) Let Φ(x) be the property: there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Since M = ⋃_i N_i is a countable union, Φ holds Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. iff, for every i, Φ holds Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. (ae_restrict_iUnion_iff). Fix i ∈ ι.

2. (Borel sets.) M is Borel, being a countable union of the Borel sets N_j (MeasurableSet.iUnion). M_i is Borel by the IMRep field measurableSet_carrier. Also N_i ⊆ M (subset_iUnion).

3. ((α) Orientation of M_i.) By the IMRep field orients of R_i, for Hᵏ⌞M_i-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_i x) Q. Since N_i ⊆ M_i, this also holds for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).

4. ((γ) N_i versus M_i inside W_i.) Apply (IMC)(a) with n := k, the open set W_i and the Borel sets N_i ⊆ M_i ⊆ W_i. Here M_i ⊆ W_i is the IMRep field carrier_subset of R_i. The finiteness hypothesis of (IMC)(a) holds: for every compact K ⊆ W_i, Hᵏ(M_i ∩ K) ≠ ∞ is the first conjunct of imrep_local_finite applied to R_i (an IMRep in W_i) and K. Hence, for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. x and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k N_i x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i x Q.

5. ((δ) N_i versus M inside U.) Apply (IMC)(a) with n := k, the open set U and the Borel sets N_i ⊆ M ⊆ U. These inclusions hold by step 2 and the hypothesis M ⊆ U. The finiteness hypothesis of (IMC)(a) is exactly the hypothesis Hᵏ(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. Hence, for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. x and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k N_i x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q.

6. ((β) The orientations agree.) By hypothesis, ξ x = ξ_i x for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. x.

7. (Combination.) The properties of steps 3–6 hold simultaneously for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. x, since finitely many full-measure sets intersect in a full-measure set (filter_upwards). Fix such an x and take Q from step 3. Then:
- Q is an approximate tangent space of M_i at x (step 3);
- hence of N_i at x (step 4, right to left);
- hence of M at x (step 5, left to right).
Also IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q holds, because ξ x = ξ_i x (step 6) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_i x) Q (step 3). So Φ(x) holds for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. x.

8. (Conclusion.) Since i was arbitrary, step 1 shows that Φ holds Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. This is the claim. ∎

subproblems.title: Gluing IMReps over countably many disjoint Borel pieces with prescribed weight μ
subproblems.statement: Assume (IMC)(a), passed as a hypothesis. It is the first hypothesis of the selected node dmcbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local_reps: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and all Borel sets M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x iff it is one of M' at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt). Let ι be a countable type, P, k ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. For each i ∈ ι let W_i ⊆ U be open, let A_i be a Borel set, and let R_i be an IMRep in W_i (IMRep (W i) k) with carrier M_i, multiplicity θ_i, orientation ξ_i and weight R_i.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M_i).withDensity θ_i (Hᵏ = μHE[k]). Assume the A_i are pairwise disjoint. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k) such that: μ(ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_i A_i) = 0; μ⌞A_i = (R_i.measure)⌞A_i for every i; μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ; and, for every i, ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) for Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ M_i ∩ A_i. Then there is an IMRep R' in U (IMRep U k) with carrier ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i), orientation R'.orient = ξ and weight R'.measure = μ.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M M' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet M' → M ⊆ M' → M' ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M' ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q) → ∀ (ι : Type) [Countable ι] (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (W A : ι → Set (Euclid P)) (R : (i : ι) → IMRep (W i) k) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsOpen U → (∀ i, IsOpen (W i)) → (∀ i, W i ⊆ U) → (∀ i, MeasurableSet (A i)) → Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (A i) (A j)) → μ (⋃ i, A i)ᶜ = 0 → (∀ i, μ.restrict (A i) = (R i).measure.restrict (A i)) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ i, ∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[k].restrict ((R i).carrier ∩ A i)), ξ y = (R i).orient y) → ∃ R' : IMRep U k, R'.carrier = ⋃ i, (R i).carrier ∩ A i ∧ R'.orient = ξ ∧ R'.measure = μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–6 and 8 of the selected node's supplied proof: the glued data (M, θ), the measure identity μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ, its consequences 6(a)–(d), and the glued IMRep of step 8. The orientation step 7 is the sibling orient_union (cbrg_ae_orient_iUnion). Everything is stated for an arbitrary countable family of pairwise disjoint Borel pieces A_i. The glued orientation is ξ itself, exactly as in the supplied proof.

Notation: Hᵏ := μHE[k]. For i ∈ ι write M_i := (R i).carrier, θ_i := (R i).mult and ξ_i := (R i).orient, so that R_i.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M_i).withDensity θ_i (contract IMRep.measure). Put N_i := M_i ∩ A_i and M := ⋃_i N_i.

The hypotheses are those of the statement: (IMC)(a); ι countable; U open; W_i open with W_i ⊆ U; A_i Borel and pairwise disjoint; μ((⋃_i A_i)ᶜ) = 0; μ⌞A_i = (R_i.measure)⌞A_i; μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ; and ξ = ξ_i holds Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e.

1. (Glued multiplicity.) Define θ : ℝ^P → ℕ as follows. If x ∈ A_j for some j, pick such a j (classical choice) and set θ(x) := θ_j(x). Otherwise set θ(x) := 0. In Lean: θ x := if h : ∃ i, x ∈ A i then (R h.choose).mult x else 0.

2. (θ = θ_i on A_i.) Let x ∈ A_i, and let j be the index chosen in step 1, so x ∈ A_j. If j ≠ i, then x ∈ A_j ∩ A_i = ∅ by pairwise disjointness, which is impossible. So j = i and θ(x) = θ_i(x). Also, θ(x) = 0 whenever x lies in no A_i.

3. (The carrier.) Each N_i = M_i ∩ A_i is Borel (field measurableSet_carrier of R_i, and A_i Borel). So M = ⋃_i N_i is Borel as a countable union. Moreover M ⊆ U, because N_i ⊆ M_i ⊆ W_i ⊆ U by the field carrier_subset and the hypothesis W_i ⊆ U.

4. (θ is measurable.) ℕ is countable with the discrete σ-algebra, so it suffices that every fibre θ⁻¹({n}) is Borel (measurable_to_countable'). By step 2,
θ⁻¹({n}) = ⋃_i (A_i ∩ θ_i⁻¹({n})) ∪ ((⋃_i A_i)ᶜ ∩ E_n),
where E_n = ℝ^P if n = 0 and E_n = ∅ otherwise. Each θ_i⁻¹({n}) is Borel by the field measurable_mult, so the right side is Borel.

5. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) If x ∈ M, then x ∈ N_i = M_i ∩ A_i for some i. So θ(x) = θ_i(x) > 0 by step 2 and the field mult_pos of R_i.

6. (M is countably k-rectifiable.) Each N_i ⊆ M_i is countably k-rectifiable by the field rectifiable of R_i and CountablyRectifiable.mono.
- If ι is empty, then M = ∅. This set is Hᵏ-null, hence countably k-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero).
- Otherwise there is a surjection s : ℕ → ι (exists_surjective_nat). Then M = ⋃_n N_{s(n)} (Function.Surjective.iUnion_comp), which is countably k-rectifiable by countablyRectifiable_iUnion.

7. (μ = Σ_i (R_i.measure)⌞A_i.) Since μ((⋃_i A_i)ᶜ) = 0, μ-a.e. point lies in ⋃_i A_i, so μ⌞(⋃_i A_i) = μ (restrict_eq_self_of_ae_mem). The A_i are pairwise disjoint Borel sets, so μ⌞(⋃_i A_i) = Σ_i μ⌞A_i (Measure.restrict_iUnion). By hypothesis μ⌞A_i = (R_i.measure)⌞A_i.

8. (The measure identity (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ = μ.) The N_i are Borel and pairwise disjoint (N_i ⊆ A_i). So Hᵏ⌞M = Σ_i Hᵏ⌞N_i (Measure.restrict_iUnion), and therefore (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ = Σ_i (Hᵏ⌞N_i).withDensity θ (withDensity_sum). For each i:
- (R_i.measure)⌞A_i = ((Hᵏ⌞M_i).withDensity θ_i)⌞A_i = (Hᵏ⌞(A_i ∩ M_i)).withDensity θ_i = (Hᵏ⌞N_i).withDensity θ_i (restrict_withDensity, Measure.restrict_restrict, commutativity of ∩);
- θ = θ_i holds Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. by step 2 and N_i ⊆ A_i, so (Hᵏ⌞N_i).withDensity θ = (Hᵏ⌞N_i).withDensity θ_i (withDensity_congr_ae).
Summing over i and using step 7 gives (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ = Σ_i (R_i.measure)⌞A_i = μ.

9. (Local integrability.) Let K ⊆ U be compact, hence closed, hence Borel. Then ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ = ((Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ)(K) (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). By step 8 this equals μ(K), which is < ∞ by hypothesis.

10. (Local finiteness of M.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hᵏ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHᵏ (setLIntegral_one). This is at most ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ, by step 5 and setLIntegral_mono (θ is measurable by step 4). By step 9 this is < ∞.

11. (ξ is Hᵏ⌞M-measurable.) θ ≠ 0 holds Hᵏ⌞M-a.e., since Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. point lies in the Borel set M and θ > 0 on M (step 5). So Hᵏ⌞M ≪ (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous'), and this measure is μ by step 8. Since ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ, it is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac).

12. (Orientation.) Apply the sibling orient_union (cbrg_ae_orient_iUnion) with (IMC)(a), ι, P, k, U, the families W, N, R and ξ. Its hypotheses hold:
- U is open and every W_i is open;
- every N_i is Borel, and N_i ⊆ M_i;
- M = ⋃_i N_i ⊆ U (step 3);
- Hᵏ(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (step 10);
- ξ = ξ_i holds Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. (hypothesis).
It yields: for Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q.

13. (The glued IMRep.) Let R' := (M, θ, ξ). Its fields are justified as follows:
- measurableSet_carrier and carrier_subset: step 3;
- rectifiable: step 6;
- measurable_mult: step 4;
- mult_pos: step 5;
- locallyIntegrable_mult: step 9;
- aestronglyMeasurable_orient: step 11;
- orients: step 12.
So R' is an IMRep in U. By construction R'.carrier = ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i) and R'.orient = ξ. By definition R'.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ, which is μ by step 8. ∎

Remark on step 11. Measurability of ξ on Hᵏ⌞M is not obtained piecewise with aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff. That lemma needs a PseudoMetrizableSpace instance for MultiVector P k = Covector →L[ℝ] ℝ, and instance synthesis does not find one in this environment (re-checked: #synth TopologicalSpace.PseudoMetrizableSpace (MultiVector 3 2) fails). So the hypothesis AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ is used instead, as in the supplied proof's step 6(d).

μ = Σ_i μ⌞A_i = Σ_i (R_i.measure)⌞A_i = Σ_i (Hᵏ⌞(M_i ∩ A_i)).withDensity θ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ (restrict_iUnion, withDensity_sum, restrict_withDensity, withDensity_congr_ae).
Hence ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ = μ(K) < ∞ and Hᵏ(M ∩ K) < ∞ on compacts K ⊆ U; Hᵏ⌞M ≪ μ gives AEStronglyMeasurable ξ (Hᵏ⌞M).
Orientation of M by ξ a.e. is the sibling orient_union applied to the pieces N_i = M_i ∩ A_i.
R' := (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U with R'.carrier = ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i), R'.orient = ξ and R'.measure = μ.
